segments.t: After Senya wishes Artyom luck in the kitchen, the young cook carries the tray up to Eleonora Andreyevna's suite. Behind closed doors, Eleonora kisses Artyom and explains her clever scheme: as long as Barinov thinks Artyom is her enemy, the chef will treat him like his own son.
Выглядит отлично! Сразу видно — рука мастера.
Да ладно!
Ну, удачи! Тебе в триста одиннадцатый номер.
Элеонора Андреевна, ваша перепёлка.
Почему так долго?
Придётся отработать!
Если честно, я не думаю, что у нас получится.
А вдруг он всё поймёт?
Не поймёт!
Пока Витя считает тебя моим врагом.
Ты будешь ему как сын родной.
Надеюсь, ты права.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Выглядит отлично! Сразу видно — рука мастера.
'It looks great! You can see right away the hand of a master.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'looks' before landing on 'master'.
Да ладно!
'Come on!' Denis brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'all right' in a few short words.
Ну, удачи! Тебе в триста одиннадцатый номер.
'Well, good luck! You are going to room three eleven.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'number' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Denis answers right away.
Элеонора Андреевна, ваша перепёлка.
'Eleonora Andreyevna, your quail.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Eleonora' before landing on 'quail'.
Почему так долго?
'Why did it take so long?' The meaning hinges on 'why' working together with 'for a long time' in spoken Russian.
Придётся отработать!
'You will have to make up for it!' Notice how Russian expresses 'it will be necessary' and 'to work off' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Denis answers right away.
Если честно, я не думаю, что у нас получится.
'To be honest, I do not think it will work out for us.' The meaning hinges on 'if' working together with 'will work out' in spoken Russian.
А вдруг он всё поймёт?
'What if he figures everything out?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'will understand' without extra filler words.
Не поймёт!
'He will not figure it out!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'not' before landing on 'will understand'.
Пока Витя считает тебя моим врагом.
'As long as Vitya considers you my enemy.' Eleonora anchors the line on 'for now', while 'enemy' completes the thought.
Ты будешь ему как сын родной.
'You will be like his own son to him.' The grammar packs 'you' and 'own' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Надеюсь, ты права.
'I hope you are right.' Notice how Russian expresses 'hope' and 'right' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

And that finishes the twist in Eleonora's suite. Listen for how Eleonora predicts that Viktor will treat Artyom like his own son as long as he considers him her enemy. Until next time!
До свидания!
